brief: Weekly Goldman Sachs equity sales roundup covering several unconnected items rather than one thesis. Earnings season: Q3 consensus EPS growth of 27% y/y, down from 33% in Q2, with AI infrastructure spending accounting for half of that growth; private-equity-stake earnings distortions should fade while tariff refunds give a modest boost; 7% of S&P 500 market cap reports next week (financials-heavy), 14% the week after. Single-stock inbounds, each independent: T/VZ/TMUS on a SpaceX spectrum deal, PLTR after an analyst upgrade to Buy, PEP after a guidance downgrade, a possible CMG/SBUX tie-up, BSP up 25% Wednesday, HUM on improved Medicare Star ratings, DAL on fuel-cost commentary. Brazil: macro attention after the election's first round, EWZ volume over $8bn Monday (more than IWM or TLT) and its largest flow on record by Thursday; GS pushes Brazil rate-sensitive and domestics baskets and notes attention on a long-EWZ/short-EUR trade. Energy: the complex is grinding higher on geopolitics; GS names 10 year-end picks across E&P, power, refining and midstream. Midterms: prediction markets imply 65% Senate odds and over 90% House odds for Democrats; historical seasonality (down pre-election, up after) sets up well for ECM into year-end.
